title: Bounded retransmission protocol (DKRT, TACAS 1997)
source: D'Argenio, Katoen, Ruys, Tretmans, 'The Bounded Retransmission Protocol must be on time!', TACAS 1997 (LNCS 1217; full version CTIT TR 97-03): the timed automata of Sec. 3.2 (Fig. 1 sender, Fig. 2 receiver) in the UPPAAL form of Sec. 4.1 (Fig. 4), the timing properties (2) and (4) of Sec. 4.2 and the timing constraint (5). The exact regions quoted in the timing rule are a reference computation with IMITATOR 3.4.0 on a transliteration of Fig. 4 (header of traceforge/examples/brp_timed.rs, lines 91 to 100; materials in docs/research/ta_problems/need-from-user-papers/brp-b04). Every v9 cell runs --model dkrt (the default).
property: One assertion, made by the main thread after it has read the summaries of sender and receiver (judge, line 908), fails when (2) is broken (the receiver takes a frame that is not a first chunk for the first frame of a new file), when (4) is broken (the sender ends its SYNC wait after a failed file while the receiver has not yet given that file up) or, with one file, when the client property is broken (one client ends with OK, the other with NOT OK); --property p2 asserts (2) alone, --property all the three together.
citable_note: Not covered by the 2026-09-18 audit (the port dates from 2026-09-19); checked here against its criteria on the current source: no mode-dependent protocol code, falsifiable properties (the timed side finds real violations one unit across each edge), timeline_impossible = 0 in every v9 run. Caveats: the boundary regions are IMITATOR's computation at n=2, MAX 1..3 and the SYNC condition of (2) is prior work (Hune et al. 2001, André et al. TACAS 2021), so the claim is exact agreement on an executable port plus precision and cost against the baseline; K=2 stands for dense time only empirically; rungs with MAX > 3 or n > 2 are beyond the range of the reference regions; the last recorded cross-validation against IMITATOR (2026-09-22) predates the send semantics of 2026-09-30.
config_timed: build_config, lines 959 to 975: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy() (960: every send may be dropped, no budget), with_progress_report(usize::MAX) (961), with_cons_type(ConsType::FIFO) (962), with_keep_going_after_error(true) when --keep-going is given (963 to 965; every v9 cell gives it), with_parallel(true).with_parallel_workers(W) when --workers W > 1 (966 to 968: the shared-queue pool; sequential otherwise), then with_timed(0, 0, 0).with_node_sd(main thread, 2^40) (973): global L=U=0 and sd=0 at sender and receiver, the main thread keeps the two summaries until it reads them. Scheduling policy not set (default LTR). Every protocol send carries its own window, in ticks: frames and acks [1, K*TD] (lines 436, 460, 658); the receiver's timer, a self-send, [K*TR-1, K*TR-1] (652); the client's offer of a file, a self-send, [0, 0] for the first file and [0, K*DC] for a later one (421, 422); the probe of (4) [0, 0] (493); Done [K*TD, K*TD] (501); the summaries [0, 0] (502, 737); the two start-up messages of main are plain sends under the global window (933, 934). Waits: the sender waits K*T1-1 ticks for an ack, then sleeps 1 (442 to 455), and sleeps K*SYNC after a failed file (491); the receiver sleeps 1 at its live timer, then reads the probe with a wait of 0 (668 to 674).
config_baseline: The same builder without with_timed (line 970): FIFO, every send may be dropped (with_all_sends_lossy, 960), keep-going and the same pool option, default LTR policy, no clock. The program is the same: the windows of its sends, its finite waits and its sleeps carry no timing information in this mode (lib.rs, documentation of with_timed).
program_differs_between_modes: no: the mode is read only in build_config (line 969) and in the summary line (line 1003); sender, receiver and judge never see it. (--model spin forces the baseline mode at line 1156, but no v9 cell uses it.)
failing_tasks: Only the main thread asserts (judge, line 908, after both threads are joined): one line main-thread-ThreadId(1) per violating execution in a sequential run, main-thread-ThreadId(N) with N naming the pool worker in a --workers run (format checked on a local run). Sender and receiver never assert. Their panic! arms are protocol errors that no v9 run reaches (the tool's count equals judged - execs in every sequential run), and the receiver's assume! (line 736) ends an execution as blocked, not as a violation.

counters.meaning: judged executions in which the monitor of (2) fired (a frame with rb1 = 0 taken in new_file). With --property p2 it equals the number of violating executions; with --property all it is one of three overlapping causes

judged executions in which the probe of (4) found the receiver still in idle. The probe is sent only with --property p4 or all, so with --property p2 this is 0 because (4) is not looked at, not because it holds
part of p2_runs: the wrongly accepted frame belongs to the file the receiver had just given up (a premature timeout, TR too small). In the summary line only
part of p2_runs: the wrongly accepted frame belongs to a later file (the new file started too early, SYNC too small). Can overlap with p2_tr_side in one execution. In the summary line only

judged executions that end with one client in OK and the other in NOT OK. A violation count only with one file and --property client or all; with F >= 2 the check is not exact, is not asserted, and the number is not zero even in holding cells. In the summary line only

executions in which the main thread reached the judgement = complete executions + violating executions (when impossible = 0). judged - execs is the number of violating executions. In the summary line only
judged executions in which a file was started after a failed one: the situation the SYNC side of (2) is about; always 0 with one file. In the summary line only
judged executions in which the receiver took a first frame after a timeout: the only place where (2) is tested non-trivially. In the summary line only
judged executions in which a probe met a receiver that had seen a frame of the failed file: a hold of (4) is informative only if this is above 0. In the summary line only
judged executions in which the sender gave at least one file up. In the summary line only
judged executions in which the receiver timed out at least once. In the summary line only
judged executions in which the sender accepted an ack that answers another frame (acks carry no bit); 0 on the timed side of every v9 cell, since T1 > 2 TD. In the summary line only
endings that admit no assignment of times (the tool's timeline_impossible); 0 in every v9 run of this example
execs + blocked + impossible, as the summary line prints it

param_columns.meaning: how often the sender resends one chunk before it gives the file up (--max)
files the sender's client offers (--files); two files are needed to exercise the SYNC side of (2)
largest transit time of a frame or an ack, in DKRT time units (--td); the transit (0, TD] is coded as [1, K*TD] ticks
sender's ack timeout in DKRT time units (--t1): without an ack it resends, or gives up, at exactly T1
receiver's timeout in DKRT time units (--tr): it gives the file up when no new frame came for TR
sender's wait after a failed file, in DKRT time units (--sync), before it may start the next file
time scale (--k): every time constant is multiplied by K to get the checker's ticks; K=2 is the half-unit grid
longest wait of the sender's client before it offers the next file, in DKRT time units; resolved default TR + TD (line 1149, no --dc given); not used with one file
derived: 2*MAX*T1 + 3*TD, the least TR for which (2) holds
derived: (2) needs it >= 0, (4) needs it > 0; 0 is the tie

worker threads of the shared-queue pool (--workers W; w1, w6, w12 in the cell names); 1 = sequential run, flag absent

boundary_law: As the source states it (header lines 10 to 13 and 91 to 100). DKRT's constraint (5), as printed, non-strict: (2) and (4) hold if T1 > 2 TD and SYNC >= TR >= 2 MAX T1 + 3 TD. Exact regions of DKRT's model (IMITATOR 3.4.0, dense time, n = 2, MAX in 1..3, T1 > 2 TD assumed, not tested): (2) holds iff TR >= 2 MAX T1 + 3 TD and SYNC + T1 >= TR + TD; (4) holds iff SYNC + T1 > TR + TD. So SYNC >= TR is sufficient, not necessary: with the TR bound, (2) and (4) both hold iff TR - SYNC < T1 - TD. With TD = 1 and T1 = 3 (every v9 cell): TR >= 6 MAX + 3; (2) needs SYNC >= TR - 2; (4) needs SYNC >= TR - 1. The client property fails in the source's tests only at T1 = 2 TD, outside every v9 cell. How well checked: the source reports 200 of 200 cross-validation runs in agreement with the IMITATOR reference of the same time grid (TR edge and (4) with one file at MAX 1..3, SYNC edge with two files at MAX 1; K = 1 and 2); K = 2 matched dense time on every cell tested, which is empirical, not proven. The last recorded run of that cross-validation is of 2026-09-22, before the send semantics of 2026-09-30, so on the campaign commit the evidence is the boundary cells: B3, B4 and C1 in v9 (C2 in v8) sit one unit on either side of each edge and the timed side reports the predicted side each time. MAX = 4 (B4) and n > 2 (D, E) are outside the range of the reference regions.

regimes.name: retransmission ladder at DKRT's safe setting, TR at its least value
regimes.params: n=2, F=1, TD=1, T1=3, TR=SYNC=2*MAX*T1+3*TD=6*MAX+3 (9, 15, 21, 27, 33, 39, 45, 51, 57 for MAX=1..9), K=2 (in ticks: transit [1,2], T1=6, TR=SYNC=12*MAX+6), property all
regimes.rule: DKRT's constraint (5) holds: T1 = 3 > 2 TD = 2 and SYNC = TR = 2 MAX T1 + 3 TD, the least TR the constraint admits (non-strict, so on the hold side); SYNC + T1 - TR - TD = 2 > 0, so (2) and (4) hold. The rungs with MAX > 3 are outside the range MAX 1..3 of the reference regions: there the expectation rests on (5), which DKRT state for every MAX, and on the measurement
regimes.expect_baseline: violations, all spurious: without a clock the receiver's timeout, the sender's waits and the transit bound are unrelated, so a late frame after a premature timeout and a probe that finds the receiver still busy cannot be ruled out

glossary.meaning: bounded retransmission protocol: a sender S sends a file as n chunks over a lossy channel, resends a chunk at most MAX times, and both clients are told whether the file got through
D'Argenio, Katoen, Ruys, Tretmans: the TACAS 1997 paper this example is ported from; a DKRT time unit is the unit of its constants TD, T1, TR, SYNC

a frame carries one chunk with the flags first, last and an alternating bit; the receiver acks every frame (acks carry no bit) and reports a frame only if its bit is the expected one, otherwise it is a duplicate
the checker's time unit: 1/K of a DKRT time unit; with K=2 a transit of (0, TD] becomes 1 to 2*TD ticks
DKRT Sec. 4.2 (2): the receiver never takes a frame that is not a first chunk for the first frame of a new file
DKRT Sec. 4.2 (4): when the sender ends its SYNC wait after a failed file, the receiver has already given that file up
DKRT Table 2 (1) and (2) for one file: the run never ends with one client told OK and the other told NOT OK
the violation when TR is too small: the receiver times out too early and a late copy of a later chunk of the same file is taken as a first frame (DKRT's Fig. 7)
the violation when SYNC is too small: the sender starts a new file while the receiver still holds the old one; needs two files
2*MAX*T1 + 3*TD: the least receiver timeout for which (2) holds (6*MAX + 3 in every v9 cell)
SYNC + T1 = TR + TD: the boundary shared by the SYNC condition of (2), which still holds there, and (4), which is already violated there
DKRT's sufficient condition: T1 > 2 TD and SYNC >= TR >= 2 MAX T1 + 3 TD
a ghost message with zero transit that the sender sends when its SYNC wait ends; it reads the receiver's location and is the monitor of (4); it is not part of the protocol
an execution in which the main thread received both summaries and evaluated the assertion

executions that end before the judgement or at a failed assertion: a dropped harness message (start-up message, file offer, timer, probe, Done, summary) leaves a blocking receive unserved, an evicted timer or probe stops the run at the receiver's guard, and under keep-going every violating execution is filed here
a violation the baseline reports in a cell where real time rules it out: the timed side reports 0
pool size in the cell names: sequential run, or --workers 6 / 12 (shared-queue pool)
a cell whose baseline was not run because it is out of reach or because it would repeat a baseline already measured (the baseline counts do not depend on the time constants)
a baseline run that is not expected to finish before the deadline; its elapsed time is a lower bound on the baseline cost
one rung above the top of a ladder, added on 2026-10-11
DKRT's own values MAX 2, TD 1, T1 3, TR 15
HOLDS or VIOLATED computed from the example's own counters, not from the tool; the workbook uses the tool's count of violating executions instead

notes: Measured numbers are those of results_v9.csv as of 2026-10-11 11:09:56. All 100 finished v9 runs of this example: exit code 0, timeline_impossible = 0, timing audit clean, complete and blocked counts identical to v8 on every side that finished in v8.

No single summary counter equals the number of violating executions, hence violation_counter is null. With --property p2 it is p2_runs. With --property all the assertion fails on (2) or (4) or the client property, the three counters overlap, and the counter of failing judged runs (ASSERT_FAIL_RUNS, line 373) is not printed. The exact relation is violating executions = judged - execs (impossible = 0): it holds in every sequential v9 run.

Counter against tool count: in the two baseline cells run with --workers 6 (A MAX=3 w6, runs brp-017; C1 w6, runs brp-009) the tool's line count is 1 to 3 below judged - execs and differs between repetitions (2811263 or 2811264 against 2811266; 1878826 or 1878827 against 1878828). Complete and blocked counts are identical. Cause not determined here (a few of the millions of lines are not counted in a parallel run); use judged - execs for these two rows.

The summary line's verdict= is counter-based. With --property all it adds p2_runs + p4_runs + client_runs (line 996), while the assertion ignores the client check when F > 1 (line 905): --files 2 or more with --property all would print VIOLATED on a holding cell. No v9 cell combines them (the two-file cells use --property p2), but client_runs is not zero in the C cells and must not be read as a violation.

The baseline counts do not depend on TD, T1, TR, SYNC or K: the four baselines at n=2, MAX=3, F=1 (A MAX=3 and the three B3 cells) agree in every counter, and in v8 the baselines of C1 at SYNC=7 and SYNC=6 agree. So the B4 cells (timed only) have the baseline of 'A MAX=4 ... w1 (headline, both >=1 min)'.

Two instances have their two sides under different cell names: the timed run of 'A MAX=5 n=2 F=1 all w1' pairs with the baseline cell 'A MAX=5 n=2 F=1 all w1 (ceiling)', and the timed run of 'C2 DKRT cell ... SYNC=13 p2 w1 (exact SYNC edge, hold)' pairs with the baseline cell 'C2 DKRT cell ... SYNC=13 p2 w1 (ceiling)'. Both ceilings did not finish in v8 and were still running in v9 at the time above.
A MAX=8 and A MAX=9 run --workers 6 on 5 pinned cores (plan column cores = 5); every other w6 cell has 6 cores and the w12 cell 12.
The time columns TD, T1, TR, SYNC, DC are in DKRT time units, as the flags and the summary line give them; the checker works in ticks = K times the value (K=2 everywhere).

The (4) verdict at the tie depends on how a wait of 0 treats a message that arrives exactly at its deadline (the probe is read with a wait of 0 at the receiver's timeout instant). The memory note project_v8_campaign records the decision of 2026-09-30 (rule A): such a message may be read or missed, for every wait including 0; one stored since before the deadline must be read. The tie cells then report (4) violated, as the strict inequality of the region says. On every cell of this example that finished under the withdrawn rule B, the rule B run, its rule A rerun and the v9 runs have identical counts.

Source against notes: the memory note brp_b04 (2026-09-19) speaks of a loss budget of at least 2 MAX; the current source has no budget, every send may be dropped in both modes (line 960). The numbers in the header comment of the source (RESULTS, items 1 and 5: for instance 102 violating runs and 11.9 M executions at the DKRT cell with SYNC=12, or 41,515 against 2,200) predate the send semantics of 2026-09-30 and partly use K=1 and judged runs as the unit; the verdicts agree with v8 and v9, the counts do not (v8: 19 violating executions, 7,808,550 explored at that cell). Take counts from the result files only.

Vacuity: in the holding cells with one file (A, D, E, B3-safe, B4-safe) no frame reaches the receiver after a timeout (first_safe_after_timeout_runs = 0) and the binary prints a NOTE saying so. With one file that is how (2) holds; the evidence that the check can fail is the adjacent B3-viol and B4-viol cells. The (4) holds are informative (probe_nontrivial_runs above 0 in every holding cell with --property all), and the two-file holds of (2) are too (restart_after_fail_runs and first_safe_after_timeout_runs above 0).

The counter-based hazard of the memory note counter_based_verdicts_hazard (counters also count endings without a timeline) does not bite here: impossible = 0 in every run, and the workbook's violating executions come from the tool's own lines.

Regime letters are the v8 prefixes of the cell names (A, B3, B4, C1, C2, D, E). A, D and E sit with TR exactly at its least value, which the non-strict TR condition puts on the hold side; they are labelled safe, and the cells one unit below (B3-viol, B4-viol) show the other side.

No v9 result yet at the time above for: the baselines of C1 w1 at SYNC=7 and SYNC=6, the timed run of A MAX=6 w1, both C2 timed cells, the baseline of D n=4, the two ceilings and the two edge rungs D n=6 and D n=7. Their expectations are the v8 results where v8 finished, else 'not measured yet'.
